meta.titre: Répondre à une question de compréhension par citation et reformulation

source.epreuve_titre: Baccalauréat séries C-D - Épreuve d'Anglais - Cameroun - Session 2000

sections.contenu_markdown: A comprehension question is never really asking 'where in the text is this mentioned?' - it is asking 'have you understood what the text means?'. Copying a sentence from the passage proves you can locate information, but it does not prove you understood it, which is exactly what examiners are checking for.

items: Basic reading skills: skimming for general meaning, scanning for specific details
Ability to identify the type of question being asked (factual, inferential, opinion-based)
Enough vocabulary to reformulate simple sentences in different words

sections.titre: The three-step method for comprehension answers
sections.contenu_markdown: For a factual or inferential question, locate the exact part of the passage that contains the answer, quote the key words as evidence (using quotation marks), then reformulate that evidence in your own words to demonstrate understanding, never leaving the quotation to stand alone as your complete answer. For a 'true or false, justify' question, state your choice as the very first word of the answer, then give one specific reason drawn from the text. For a personal-opinion question, give a clear, unambiguous position (do not sit on the fence) and support it with at least one concrete reason, ideally connected to an idea raised in the passage itself.
sections.formule_principale: \text{Locate} \to \text{Quote as evidence} \to \text{Reformulate in your own words}

sections.enonce_markdown: Passage: '...sperm lasts only so long, but a sperm factory can, in theory, go on forever.' Question: Stem cells are more reliable for reproductive regeneration than sperm. True or false? Justify.

etapes.action: State the choice clearly as the first word
etapes.justification: The examiner must see the position immediately, without ambiguity
The passage directly contrasts the two methods
etapes.resultat_markdown: The text states that '"sperm lasts only so long, but a sperm factory can, in theory, go on forever"'

etapes.action: Reformulate the evidence in your own words
etapes.justification: This shows understanding rather than simple copying
etapes.resultat_markdown: In other words, frozen sperm has a limited usable lifespan, whereas stem cells can keep regenerating themselves indefinitely, which makes them more durable and reliable

sections.conclusion_markdown: A complete answer states the choice, quotes the evidence, and reformulates it: 'True. The text explains that frozen sperm "lasts only so long", whereas a stem-cell-based sperm factory "can, in theory, go on forever" because stem cells can keep renewing themselves, which makes them a more reliable, long-lasting source.'

items.erreur_markdown: Answering with a direct copy of a full sentence from the passage and nothing else
items.pourquoi_faux: This proves only that the candidate can locate information in the text, not that they understood it; many marking schemes explicitly withhold marks for pure copying without any reformulation.
items.correction_markdown: Always add at least one sentence, in your own words, that restates the quoted evidence or explains what it means, even if the reformulation is simple.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving a vague or hedging answer to a 'true or false' or personal-opinion question ('it depends', 'maybe both')
items.pourquoi_faux: These question types specifically require a clear, committed position; an answer that refuses to choose cannot be properly assessed against the marking scheme.
items.correction_markdown: Force yourself to choose one clear position as your very first sentence, even if the topic feels genuinely balanced: you can acknowledge nuance afterwards, but you must commit to an answer first.

items.enonce_markdown: Passage: 'The new machine works twice as fast as the old one, but it also uses twice as much electricity.' Question: Is the new machine cheaper to run than the old one? Justify.
items.solution_markdown: 'It is not necessarily cheaper. The text says the new machine "uses twice as much electricity" even though it works faster, so any time saved may be offset by higher electricity costs.'

items.enonce_markdown: Passage: 'Many students give up learning a language after only a few months because they expect to become fluent too quickly.' Question: Why do many students abandon language learning early, according to the text?
items.solution_markdown: 'According to the text, many students give up because they "expect to become fluent too quickly". In other words, their unrealistic expectations about how fast they should progress lead to disappointment, which causes them to stop.'

items.enonce_markdown: Passage: '...as a result, says the researcher, "we may one day be able to grow entire organs from a patient's own cells".' Question: Do you think this kind of research should be funded by governments? Justify your opinion.
items.solution_markdown: 'Yes, I believe this research should be funded. The text suggests it could allow doctors to "grow entire organs from a patient's own cells", which would save countless lives currently lost to organ shortages, and using a patient's own cells would also reduce the risk of organ rejection, making the treatment safer than traditional transplants.'

items_markdown: A comprehension answer always follows three steps: locate the evidence, quote it, then reformulate it in your own words.
Never let a direct quotation stand alone as your complete answer.
For 'true or false, justify' questions, state your choice as the first word of your answer.
For personal-opinion questions, commit to a clear position and support it with at least one concrete, ideally text-connected, reason.
